notes: On a customer's Identity tab, the Findings and Categories cards now report the same number of categories (matching the tabs below), and clicking the Critical or High card jumps you straight to the relevant findings instead of force-opening one.
Finding drill-downs now match the rest of the portal: every column shows it can be sorted at a glance (not only on hover), and the 'How to fix' guides use the standard squared step markers and type.

On a customer's Identity tab, the Findings and Categories cards now report the same number of categories (matching the tabs below), and clicking the Critical or High card jumps you straight to the relevant findings instead of force-opening one.
Finding drill-downs now match the rest of the portal: every column shows it can be sorted at a glance (not only on hover), and the 'How to fix' guides use the standard squared step markers and type.

A customer's Activity log no longer scrolls on forever: it now shows the 10 most recent events with a 'Show more' button to expand (and 'Show fewer' to collapse), plus a running 'Showing X of Y' count. Switching the bundle or action filter resets it to the latest 10.

New currency selector in the top bar: switch the whole portal between NOK (default), SEK, DKK, EUR, USD and GBP. License cost and waste figures convert instantly; your actual Stripe billing stays in NOK.
License Insights is clearer: the SKU inventory now shows clean product names with an Active / Stale / Unassigned colour key, sharper utilisation bars and larger, more legible figures.

The per-customer Cost trend is now a sparkline card matching the fleet overview — smooth line, subtle glow and a hover tooltip — and the Reclaim candidates' recommended action reads as a proper status tag.

Fleet overview redesigned: each KPI card now draws its own trend as a smooth, colour-coded sparkline; Open cases moved up under the cards for faster triage; and Alert volume is now an on-demand overlay where you can show, hide or isolate any incident category.

Customer Overview cards refreshed: colour-coded Active alerts, Identity findings, Conditional Access (policy count + guard mode) and Last backup — replacing the old Bundles and the duplicate Last-sync tile.

Polish throughout: incident owners always resolve to a name instead of a raw id, the customer search dropdown matches the portal (no typewriter font or off-palette blue), the Identity Health and Conditional Access tables breathe better, and scrollbars are themed to the dark UI.
Customers: the tenant ID now renders in JetBrains Mono, so the GUID's glyphs (0/O, 1/l/I) read unambiguously — easier to scan and copy — while the column spacing stays exactly where it was.

Inbox triage at fleet scale: a default 'By priority' view (most-critical first, so a Critical is never hidden) and an opt-in 'By customer' view that groups cases per tenant — worst-first, with a per-customer severity rollup and the customers that need action auto-expanded. Every column stays sortable, like the other tables.
Customers list: even breathing room across the left columns — the gap between Customer and Health now matches the Health-to-Status gap, and the table still fits narrower windows without clipping.

Customers list: more breathing room between the Customer, Health and Status columns (the 'Billing' column is now 'Status'), Health sits a little further to the right, and the Alerts column is a clean count instead of a dot.
Opening an incident now shows the same severity tag as the rest of the portal (the High orange), instead of an off-palette one.
Severity tags now read as a proper heat scale — Critical (red) and High (orange) are clearly distinct, then Medium (amber) and Low (grey).

Sorting is consistent across every list now: all columns are click-sortable through one shared header. Customers' Billing, the Inbox incident column, and the Backup and Licenses fleet tables are now sortable too (their default order is unchanged until you click a header).
Design polish: the “High” severity tag now matches the others (filled, not outlined), and every column on the Identity Health and Conditional Access lists clearly shows it can be sorted.

The portal-wide design refresh is complete: section headings, tables and the last status tags are now aligned across Settings, Licenses, Billing, Backup and the incident pages — every page follows one consistent system.
A cleaner, more consistent look across the portal: every status tag — health, billing, severity, backup and more — now shares one style, and the columns line up.

Calmer charts: the identity and conditional-access breakdowns and the alert-volume chart use a coordinated, muted palette instead of loud primary colours, so they read as data rather than alarms. Status colours (like red “Critical”) are kept where they carry meaning.

Customers you’ve just connected now show “Pending” on the Customers list until their first security scan completes — instead of an alarming “Warning”. It clears to a real Healthy, Warning or Critical status on its own, usually within minutes.
Hover a customer’s Health status to see what it means in plain language, plus that customer’s own open finding counts — critical, high, medium, low — and the risk score behind it.
Incident owners now show the analyst's name instead of an internal ID — across the inbox list, open cases and the incident page.
Manage subscription in Stripe now opens in a new tab, so you stay in the portal while updating billing and payment details.
In-app notifications now match the portal's design — the same card surface, the standard green check, and squared corners.
New Backup & Restore section: see your whole fleet's backup health at a glance — protected, stale, or no backup — and jump straight to any tenant's restore page.
Settings is tidier: Billing and Backup now have their own top-level sections instead of living inside Settings, which goes back to just configuration.
When a new customer grants consent, the welcome page now greets them by their organisation name and domain instead of a raw tenant ID.
Active tenants now have every feature fully working: the Identity, Conditional Access and Licenses tabs unlock AND load their data the moment a tenant is activated.
The 'No tenants active yet' banner clears once at least one tenant is active.
Active tenants now unlock every feature: the Identity, Conditional Access and Licenses tabs open as soon as a tenant is activated - no more locked tabs after you've paid.
The 'No tenants active yet' banner clears once at least one tenant is active.
New per-tenant billing: onboard tenants for free, then activate the ones you want from the Activate tenants page - each priced by its measured size. Replaces buying bundles and assigning seats.
One Basewiser product: Conditional Access Vault, Identity Health and License Insights are now a single product with every feature included.
Cleaner billing: the old per-tenant bundle-assignment page is gone - activation is the single, simpler flow.
Copying an invite now confirms it worked - Copy email, the consent link and the App ID show a 'Copied' tick when you click them.

The 'Set up the Basewiser app' step adds a plain-language 'What this does' explainer (the app and its credentials stay in your own Microsoft Entra tenant, each customer approves it once, you get read-only visibility plus Conditional Access remediation), and the setup button matches the rest of the portal.

Onboarding step 1 now checks off with a green tick and stays aligned with step 2 once the Basewiser app is set up - showing the app's name and ID without a heavy card. The setup button matches the portal's other buttons.
Once the Basewiser app is set up, the confirmation matches the version-update banner - a single blue mark with the app's name and ID - instead of a green 'Active' card.
The Add-tenant dialog buttons now match the rest of the portal - calm neutral buttons instead of a bold blue fill.

The email-invite instructions are clearer and harder to misread: labelled Option 1 (email the invite) and Option 2 (just send the link), step-by-step guidance that names each button and your mail app (e.g. Outlook), and a 'What this does' summary of what you send and what the customer's Global Administrator approves.

The email invite now says where it sends - Open in mail launches a new message in your default mail app (Outlook, etc.) - and adds a 'What this does' explainer covering what you send, what the customer's Global Admin approves, and what Basewiser can (and can't) see.
You can also just share the consent link instead of sending the full email - over Teams, chat, or an existing thread.

Sending an email invite now spells out the steps - copy the email, open a new message, paste it in - and adds an 'or just send the link' option for sharing the consent link over Teams, chat or an existing thread.
The invite email itself is redesigned: clearer layout with the Basewiser wordmark, a stronger call-to-action button, and labelled sections (it reads well in both light and dark mail clients).
Once the Basewiser app is set up, the panel states it's been created and ready to onboard tenants, and lists the app's name and App ID.
The first-run setup screen now matches the rest of the portal - same components, and once the Basewiser app is set up it shows the green Active panel with the app's name and App ID.

The Add-tenant dialog is polished and consistent with the rest of the portal: once the Basewiser app is set up it shows as an Active panel with the app's name and App ID (copyable), and the email-invite step is a single 'Open in mail' action that carries the branded message.
Invite emails render correctly in dark mode now (Outlook included) - the Basewiser wordmark adapts to the reader's theme instead of washing out.
First-run setup: opening a fresh portal now walks you through naming your organisation (the name customers see on invites) and setting up the Basewiser app - one screen, two steps.
After setup, the onboarding dialog shows your Basewiser app's name and App ID, with a spinner while it provisions.
Invite emails are branded now: Copy email gives you a formatted Basewiser message to paste into your mail client, and the invite reminds you which Partner identity it's sent as.
If app setup fails, the dialog names the exact Microsoft Graph permission the backend needs.
The onboarding dialog now notices if you delete the Basewiser app in Entra - it flips back to 'set up needed' instead of staying stuck on active, so you can re-create it cleanly.

Sending an email invite opens your own mail app with the subject and message (including the consent link) already filled in - just add recipients from your contacts and send. The in-portal recipient box is gone.
Polish: the two onboarding method cards line up, and the empty-state 'Add your first tenant' button is neutral grey like the rest of the portal.

Adding a tenant is now a guided two-step flow: set up the Basewiser app once (it's the single app every managed tenant consents to - one consent screen per customer instead of one per feature), then onboard tenants by branded email invite or directly. The onboarding panel is wider and spells out what each choice is for.
If app setup hits an error, the dialog now shows the actual reason inline instead of the button appearing to do nothing.
Partner identity (Settings) is simpler: set your display name and a support contact for tenant invite emails - the logo field is gone, invites use Basewiser branding.

Adding a tenant now starts with a choice, right from the Add tenant button: send a branded email invite the customer's own admin approves in one click, or add the tenant directly when you already hold an admin account in it.

New Onboarding page: connect a managed tenant two ways - onboard it directly when you hold an admin account in it, or generate a branded email invite that the customer's own admin approves in one click. Either way, the tenant registers itself in the portal once consent is granted.
Onboarding now runs on a single Basewiser app, so each customer approves one consent screen instead of one per feature.
Set the name customers see on the invite under Settings - Partner identity; it's pre-filled from your subscription and editable.
The tenant ID on Customers only copies from the copy icon now - the id itself is plain, selectable text, so a stray click no longer copies it.
Table columns are spread evenly across the width - the reclaim queue, fleet licensing and the licensing report no longer leave a big gap before the right-hand columns.
Status and empty-state icons now match the portal's squared corners - the 'all clear' check and the case-status glyphs (resolved, new) are squared instead of round.

Text across the portal is easier to read: descriptions, names, email and sign-in addresses, tenant IDs and other body text now sit at a consistent, comfortable size with a readable colour floor, instead of fine print. The break-glass section and the dense detail pages benefit most.
Layout lines up: the tenant detail and Zero Trust pages now use the same wide column as the rest of the portal, and the update / license banners match the page width instead of floating narrower.
On Customers, the tenant ID shows in full again - monospace, click to copy - instead of being cropped mid-string.
Selected filters are readable again - the active state is now a calm neutral highlight instead of blue text on a blue fill, across the Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access.

The Customers and Inbox lists read as a single table now, with the column header attached to its rows like Identity and Licenses. Inbox rows are calmer too: verdict tags (Auto-restored, Review sign-ins, GA) line up in their own column instead of crowding the title, the owner always shows a name rather than a raw id, and the description is trimmed so tenant, owner and age have room.

More squared-corner polish and faster triage: avatars and the resolved check-marks pick up the portal's squared corners, the Identity health summary cards are clickable (click Critical to filter to critical findings, worst first), the Licenses cards match the rest of the portal, and customer tenant IDs show a short head…tail you can click to copy the full id.

Every incident now tells its change story as a ledger on the affected policy: baseline, while the change was live, and now - with counts first (+ 5 excluded), names on demand, and the outcome stated outright (all removed - back at baseline). Readable in seconds even for big changes.
What-changed slims to the verdict and the raw diff - the story is told once, right next to the live state it explains. Timeline icons now match the portal's squared corners.

The incident page is redesigned: a calmer header with the owner shown by name (never a raw object-id), and Live policy state as a flat spec sheet - assignments collapse to clickable type counts and expand to a searchable list showing display names and sign-in addresses.
Small grey text across the portal is raised to a readable floor - sign-in addresses, owner names and customer tenant ids are no longer micro-print.
Audit attribution now records the operator's email even when the sign-in only carried a display name.
The 'update available' banner is calmer and gently animated, and the What's-new window is now a release timeline - every release since your version, newest first, with its change count.
Installing an update now shows real progress with an estimated time remaining instead of a plain spinner.

The Fleet overview is rebuilt: richer stat cards with honest trend badges, an alert-volume chart that stacks the four incident categories (Privilege escalation, Policy guard, Identity hygiene, Operations) from your real investigation log over the selected window, and an Open-cases table linking straight into each incident.
The whole portal now uses wide screens: the dashboard, Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access pages widen to the same cap the incident page got - more data, fewer dead margins.
Status gets a face: open cases carry the new status pill (dashed circle = new, spinner = in progress, green check = resolved) - the first piece of the refreshed component language.
Tab strips across the portal hug their content again instead of stretching edge to edge - the compact form reads better on wide screens.

What's new now accumulates: skip a release and its notes carry into the next banner. The portal shows everything since YOUR running version, grouped per release - no more updates silently replacing the notes you never read.

The incident page uses big screens properly: evidence and impact cards take the extra width while the playbook and timeline keep their comfortable size - no more content squeezed between dead margins.
Quiet polish: tab count badges stay the same calm grey whether or not the tab is active - selection reads from the tab itself. Severity-tinted finding counts keep their red and amber.

The Basewiser B is now the browser tab icon - the brand mark on a card tile matching the portal design, crisp from pinned tabs up to full-size bookmarks. If your tab still shows the old icon, a hard refresh clears the cached one.

The inbox is rebuilt for triage: every incident is its own card with sortable columns (severity, tenant, owner, age), an incident category on each row (Privilege escalation, Policy guard, Identity hygiene, Operations), and a quick-actions menu - assign to me, take over, open the customer, copy the link - without opening the case.

Filters speak one language everywhere: multi-select pills with built-in search and one-click clear on the Inbox, Customers, Identity health and Conditional Access pages. Filter to two tenants and a category in three clicks; the X on the pill undoes it in one.

The Customers list gains search and sortable columns - sort by Alerts for the what's-on-fire view - and secondary tab rows across the portal are now full-width segmented strips, with the Identity tab reclaiming the space the old side table-of-contents held.

Role-grant alerts no longer reference an allowlist - there is no role allowlist; severity is purely tier-driven (GA above Tier 0, other roles lower). The change allowlist keeps governing guard-mode alerts, where it belongs.

Granter resolution is now three layers deep: the admin's own audit footprint resolves instantly, PIM schedule requests confirm intent (activation vs admin grant), and granter-less rows backfill for 24 hours - the WHO tile updates itself with a journal note.
Findings move with events: a role grant triggers the tenant's identity rescan immediately, and the active-alert badge updates the moment an incident is resolved.

Incident owners now resolve to a real name even when it wasn't captured at assignment: the backend looks the operator up in your team directory, so the inbox and Open cases show a person instead of an object id.
